findings.function: obtainDepositData(uint256,bytes), allocateDeposits(...), finalizeUpgradeV2() and the other writers of slot 9
findings.decompiled: stor9 = stor9 & 0xffffffffffffffff0000000000000000ffffffffffffffff0000000000000000 | uint64(-_4 + uint64(stor9 >> 128)) << 128 | uint64(_4 + uint64(stor9)); while idx < stor9 >> 192
findings.source: BaseModule storage $.nodeOperatorsCount / deposited and depositable counters packed in one slot (uint64 fields)
findings.issue: The packed slot 9 (four uint64 counters) is declared as one uint256 and read and written with shifts and masks in 63 lines, so `nodeOperatorsCount` appears only as `stor9 >> 192` (P15).
findings.rule: Split a slot into fields when every access is a shift/mask of disjoint bit ranges, and print the read-modify-write as separate field assignments.

notes: Lido CuratedModule (solc 0.8.33, osaka, no via-IR) with 7 linked external libraries (50 delegatecalls: deposit allocator, node-operator ops, withdrawn-validator lib...), whose loops are not in this bytecode. Source loops in this bytecode, all shown as readable whiles: finalizeUpgradeV2 (542), SigningKeys.loadKeys in getSigningKeys (832), SigningKeys.loadKeysSigs in getSigningKeysWithSignatures (1221) and obtainDepositData (2330), batchDepositInfoUpdate (1369), settleGeneralDelayedPenalty (1740), getDepositsAllocation (1814), obtainDepositData's allocation loop (`while True` with the exit test first, 2299), allocateDeposits (2402). The other 36 whiles are implicit ABI encodes/decodes, including the struct-array encodes of WithdrawnValidatorInfo[] into library delegatecalls (P7). Some events (e.g. topic 0x7220970e... at 2306) show their data as `mem[mem[64] len ...]` (free-pointer identification, see c00026). Small view functions and access-control paths read correctly.
summary: Good text: every source loop in the bytecode is a readable while and the semantics look intact; the remaining noise is implicit ABI copy loops, a packed counter slot handled as raw bit arithmetic, and a few raw-memory event payloads.
